No not yet Is it still experiencing problems? From what i can tell my validators are still attesting just fine Yes, we suspect that there is an issue with prysm-geth proposing blocks is this also a tooling issue with blcok explorers We need ... client diverse beacon chain explorers ... beaconcha.in is dependent on prysm... <@!474028048551772160> thats a good point more options in this area would be great why is beaconcha.in limited to Prysm only? I seem to see a lighthouse implementation for their RPC? The beaconchain fork we use is reliant on lighthouse. but its crashing due to an issue with the indexer. I'm only going off what the documentation says. Its possible that lighthouse has the needed api's now, but it isn't documented. Is there a bad block command on the CL? On the EL if we get a block that we can not execute, we store it in the bad block database s.th. we can easily debug it later on. Do you guys have something similar? LH logs the block ssz with if run with trace logs Lodestar has a folder in its data called 'invalidSszObjects' I'm going to stop working on it for now, I believe that there is an issue in prysm that modifies the block data between block creation and block execution Other geth nodes look fine and other client combinations also look ok afaik There are several files there under 2022-03-15 interesting my besu/teku pair seems to be stuck on block 55129 <@!583892532644151312> > Teku incorrectly ignores our incorrect INVALID_BLOCK_HASH and keeps resending it anyone from Teku can help debugging/fixing? <@&836981489430036500> Yeah, it seems that Erigon incorrectly sends INVALID_BLOCK_HASH for correct NewPayload height=55186 hash=0x0e802ab0f7cfdf90886c785397d8dd4788e52e5370fc52059ddd06e09767d33b, but then teku ignores our reply and keeps resending the same payload. Looks like this block got an incorrect baseFeePerGas, it has 1770307273, and calculating the hash, you get the value geth expected 0x4939674c8df87bbf80d2a6fbe337cc54c63d92bd016e734cf2c53f719a39bfe2, but if you substitute the base fee with 3384706153 (actual base fee expected for that block), the hash is now what we see in the block's `blockHash` field: 0xc7b7ba871a2628dbc765ace5183af24fc9915ec453375821833665c9536f1041 cc <@!363800010518822915> Thanks friends! I also can confirm that everything works on.`gcr.io/prysmaticlabs/prysm/beacon-chain:kiln-4724b8` (devnet5 build), The latest `gcr.io/prysmaticlabs/prysm/beacon-chain:kiln-ee1ee6` has issues. Easier to spot out the offenders now... Just fighting a different fire at the moment, but we'll take a look as soon as possible. Thanks! 1770307273 = 0110 1001 1000 0100 1011 1110 1100 1001 3384706153 = 1100 1001 1011 1110 1000 0100 0110 1001 Looks a lot like big vs little endian to me <@!363800010518822915> 6984BEC9 vs C9BE8469 Thats also why the bad blocks are not happening anymore, too little transactions, the basefee is 7 -> equal regardless of endianness ah i see, I was banging my head on why this didn't show up on devnet5 with older commits, maybe it's always 7 there ``` 1770307273 = 0110 1001 1000 0100 1011 1110 1100 1001 3384706153 = 1100 1001 1011 1110 1000 0100 0110 1001 ``` Looks like all of the testing and reporting action is happening in this channel instead of <#910910348922589184> It appears that the the PoW chain re-orged deeper than the `ETH1_FOLLOW_DISTANCE` before the transition. Hey, I'm querying the consensus layer bacon API to get the validators.
And what I get is objects like this:
```
ValidatorData {
    index: 105995,
    balance: 31014069414,
    status: ExitedSlashed,
    validator: Validator {
        pubkey: 0xa08728ac903ca30ccf168448b8947e2593ccf6d2d24fccd273ea90cc1aada19643516f41030e2fbece52311a6c88373b,
        withdrawal_credentials: 0x00a6ee388ab2fe78209c6b3a2d65794a842b3cfd4d131f2f506b70167c59bd75,

        slashed: true,
        activation_eligibility_epoch: Epoch(627),
        activation_epoch: Epoch(638),
        exit_epoch: Epoch(760),
        withdrawable_epoch: Epoch(8947),

```

Basically, can I flatten this object to store it in DB, or is there a one-to-many relation between validator and ValidatorData ?
